title: Excalidraw toolbar comparison lab
summary: Big and touch friendly stays the default. Try three new versions that explore what happens after drawing, what fits on a portrait tablet, and how to show shortcuts without losing labels.

variations.name: Minimal and calm
variations.idea: Four labeled essentials stay visible; More tools holds the rest, and Repeat tool makes retention explicit.

variations.name: Playful and expressive
variations.idea: Pick from a hand-drawn palette that shows what each tool does and whether it stays active after drawing.

variations.name: Dense for power users
variations.idea: Every tool and its real shortcuts at a glance, with tool retention and everyday commands in the same compact strip.

variations.name: Big and touch friendly
variations.idea: A thumb-reachable dock keeps Select, Pan, Insert image, and Repeat tool visible above a labeled drawing grid on narrow screens.
variations.why: Labels and generous tap targets stay. Repeat tool shows On or Off, and the active tool gets an outline so selection doesn't depend on color.

variations.name: Draw Again
variations.idea: A control next to the drawing tools says whether you'll keep using that tool or switch back to Select.

video.title: Draw Again: five circles without reselecting Ellipse

variations.name: Portrait Dock
variations.idea: Keep Insert image and core tools in reach, and put the rest one tap away.

video.title: Portrait Dock: find a core tool and open the secondary tools

variations.name: Labels + Shortcuts
variations.idea: Keep plain-language labels and reveal shortcut keys inside the existing buttons, without widening the dock.

video.title: Labels + Shortcuts: reveal the keys and draw with R and O
